audit_findings.title: Consolidated VIE cash flows may not belong to KRT common shareholders
audit_findings.mechanism: Unallocated Global Wells cash-flow adjustments could inflate recurring OE, while VIE cash or other assets could also be overstated in the equity bridge; every $1.0m recurring anchor-OE overstatement corresponds to approximately $14.05m of base operating PV, or $0.69 per share.
audit_findings.evidence: The monthly lease payments for both the Texas Lease and New Jersey Lease are eliminated upon consolidation.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that KRT owns only 15.1% of Global Wells, consolidates it, eliminates the Texas and New Jersey lease payments, and reported $1.186m of 2025 income attributable to noncontrolling interests. They do not establish whether the OE workpapers started with income attributable to KRT and correctly allocated consolidated D&A, capex, and working-capital adjustments. Because any recurring error is capitalized throughout the forecast and terminal value, the issue is reasonably capable of materially changing intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct every OE year from net income attributable to Karat Packaging Inc.; identify all Global Wells D&A, capex, working-capital changes, rent eliminations, and cash; allocate each item according to KRT's economic claim and rerun all scenarios and the bridge.

audit_findings.title: The bridge may classify operating liquidity as excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; up to $54.143m is classified as excess, equal to $2.66 per share and 11.6% of the $467m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash required for inventory, letters of credit, debt maturity, leases, or ordinary working capital supports forecast OE and cannot simultaneously be added as a distributable non-operating asset in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We currently believe that our cash on hand, ongoing cash flows from our operations and funding available under our borrowings will be adequate to meet our working capital needs, service our debt, make lease payments, and fund capital expenditures for at least the next 12 months.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge demonstrably adds the entire $54.143m cash-and-short-term-investment balance, but the record does not demonstrate that this entire balance is excess. A substantial operating requirement is plausible because June 2026 current liabilities were $88.551m, inventory was $89.085m, standby letters of credit were $16.431m, remaining revolver availability was only $3.569m, and the $11.372m 2026 term loan was approaching maturity. The maximum amount at issue is large enough to materially change the reported intrinsic value and buy-below threshold.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 2026 parent and subsidiary cash schedules; separate unrestricted cash from VIE cash and any pledged or operationally committed balances; calculate minimum cash using monthly working-capital seasonality, letter-of-credit requirements, lease payments, the September 2026 debt maturity, dividends, and committed capital spending; then rerun the bridge using only demonstrated excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Customs exposure could exceed the recorded claim against equity
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified incremental exposure above the $1.291m reserve at 2026-06-30; filed payments through that date totaled $2.097m
audit_findings.mechanism: Any final customs assessment above amounts already recognized in OE or liabilities is a one-time cash claim senior to common equity and should reduce the valuation bridge or the applicable historical OE adjustment.
audit_findings.evidence: The amount of the final payments could vary significantly from the estimated liability reserve.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability is demonstrated, but an omitted loss above the recorded amount is not. The latest filing shows a $1.291m reserve, down from $1.720m at year-end, and states that final payments could vary significantly; it supplies no reasonably estimable upper bound. Consequently, the record cannot establish the incremental magnitude or whether it is material to the $467m base equity value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every CBP bill, protest determination, accrued-interest amount, payment, and remaining shipment through September 6, 2026; obtain counsel's exposure range; verify what was already charged through historical OE; and rerun the bridge for any probable or reasonably estimable amount not already captured.

audit_findings.title: The low-capex operating model may not persist
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed capital spending including equipment deposits was $4.505m in 2025 versus $10.891m of D&A, and $2.274m in the first half of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher normalized maintenance or tariff-mitigation capital expenditure would reduce future OE and could also reduce sustainable growth if reinvestment requirements exceed those embedded in the forecast.
audit_findings.evidence: Although we have recently shifted towards an asset light model by increasing import and scaling back production and reducing capital expenditure, changes in economic and political conditions may result in us incurring significant capital expenditures again to expand manufacturing.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate low recent capital spending and disclose that political or economic changes could require renewed manufacturing and other infrastructure investment. They do not demonstrate a present commitment or provide a quantified future spending requirement. This is therefore a forward-looking risk to monitor rather than a presently demonstrated valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Build a full-cycle maintenance-capex schedule by asset class and compare it with depreciation, asset age, disposals, and capacity; obtain committed warehouse, fleet, systems, and manufacturing projects; then stress OE for a domestic-production or tariff-mitigation case if management commits to renewed investment.
